items.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997
items.q: And then my main trio after a couple of months was Bill Crow and Joe Morello.

ctx.x: So I guess I mean if I think of it now I mean I remember mostly the good things, because I had a great trio. Well actually for openers I had a guy named Mel Zelnick and I’m trying to think who the bass player was, that’s awful I can’t think, but anyway I think we had Vinnie Burke for a while. And then my main trio after a couple of months was Bill Crow and Joe Morello. And I mean that was the main trio for about three or four years.

items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I used to work there with Marian McPartland.

ctx.x: Wasn’t that the story with Freddie Keppard? And he passed up the chance to be the first Dixieland group?

Yeah. Wouldn’t record. But as soon as people began to realize that then to get a record was important if you wanted to be a popular band, and to get a job in a club that had a radio wire at night was important. That was one of the big things that built the bands at the Hickory House. I used to work there with Marian McPartland. But in the years before that, when they were first starting out, at night, they didn’t have a whole lot of sponsored programs. So all the radio stations would put telephone wires into the…
So when did you arrive in New York, officially?

items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: finally arrived at this good trio with Bill Crow and Joe Morello. That was the . . . one of the good groups I had in there.

ctx.x: In fact when you take that tape home. It’s funny, there’s a couple of tunes on there I wrote at the Hickory House. They’re really not bad. At the time I was scared to play this tune. In fact this will give you a laugh, because I didn’t even want to say that I’d written the tune, because I was sure I would get criticized by Bill Crow, who was very . . . He always liked to come forward with a remark. He’d probably say, “I don’t care about playing that” or something. So I didn’t let on that I’d written this tune. I…
